facts.title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Large Reasoning Models: A Preregistered Two-Harness Benchmark of Coding Agents
facts.event_hint: Preregistered benchmark of prompt and harness effects on coding-agent reasoning cost
facts.problem: Reasoning-model coding agents spend on hidden deliberation, tool calls, repeated turns, and static harness prefixes, but prompt folklore does not reveal which costs improve correctness. Billing cache rebates can further hide behavioral inefficiency, so prompt and harness effects need controlled measurement.
facts.mechanism: The benchmark freezes 24 deterministic coding tasks, hidden evaluators, prompt variants, six reasoning models, and two real harnesses. It pairs conditions while measuring reasoning tokens, tool calls, turns, inspected files, duplicate reads, time, scope violations, success, and cached versus uncached billing. A bounded-efficiency prompt explicitly sets scope, acceptance criteria, smallest-sufficient change, and a stop condition; deep-thinking and multi-approach prompts are tested against it.

evidence.claim: Asking the model to develop and compare several approaches multiplies reasoning tokens by 2.4–7.4x on every model with no correctness gain.
evidence.condition: Six large reasoning models; holdout-confirmed on eight unseen tasks

evidence.claim: Generic deep-thinking cues increase deliberation by 1.6–2.2x and roughly double wall time with identical tool behavior.
evidence.condition: Models where the feature was selected; replicated across pilot, screening, and holdout

evidence.claim: A bounded-efficiency template is neutral-or-better on all six models and halves GLM-5.2 reasoning at equal success.
evidence.condition: Holdout tasks with explicit scope, acceptance criteria, and stop condition

evidence.claim: Identical model-task-prompt triples cost 5–30x more per success under Claude Code than PI.DEV, driven by a 12–15x larger static prefix and 2–7x more turns.
evidence.condition: Matched pilot task/prompt/model cells with approximately 100% success
evidence.source_locator: PDF pages 1 and 4, Abstract and Section 4.3

evidence.claim: Provider-side prefix caching rebated about 61% of estimated no-cache billing without changing behavioral metrics.
evidence.condition: Automatic provider-side prefix cache over benchmark phases

facts.evaluation_context: A preregistered benchmark used 24 deterministic multi-language coding tasks with hidden evaluators, six reasoning models served by Together AI, and PI.DEV versus Claude Code harnesses. It covered 4,643 valid runs and separated behavioral metrics from cached/uncached billing; replications included Kimi-K3 and first-party Claude Sonnet 5.
facts.limitations: The main benchmark uses deterministic read/modify coding fixtures, selected models, and two harnesses; effects may differ on open-ended software work, other providers, or newer harness versions. The Claude Code cost comparison includes a large fixed prefix and turn behavior specific to the harness setup. Provider cache hits are probabilistic and can distort billing comparisons; Anthropic's API does not separately report thinking tokens, requiring total-output-token ratios there. The abstract does not establish causal effects on every tool-call type or repository scale (inference).
facts.project_relevance: Agent delegation should use explicit scope, acceptance criteria, exact output contracts, and stop conditions: these are cost-neutral or cheaper while reducing the chance of open-ended reasoning. Harness overhead and silent gateway metadata loss make model/prompt comparisons unreliable without capturing raw usage and validating a real multi-step tool loop; cache rebates must be kept separate from behavioral efficiency (inference).
